item.title: Monday Morning Headlines: Incoming Storm Tuesday
item.description: Another atmospheric river is coming our way; BART is blaming Sunday's massive service meltdown on a street-level fire; and Supreme Court Justice Samuel Alito is rumored to be mulling retirement.

item.title: Apartment Fire on Nob Hill Leaves One Injured
item.description: An early morning fire left one person injured on Nob Hill Monday, and it's unclear how badly they were injured.

item.title: Body of Man Found In Lake Berryessa Suspected to Be Victim of Kidnapping
item.description: After 57-year-old Avtar Singh was reported missing in Tracy last Tuesday, authorities have confirmed that a body found in Lake Berryessa on Friday is his, and surveillance video indicates foul play by three suspected kidnappers.

item.title: California Tourists Stranded In Puerto Vallarta and Other Mexican Cities as Cartel Wreaks Revenge for Slain Leader
item.description: Many flights in and out of Puerto Vallarta and other Mexican cities were canceled on Sunday, amid a wave of arson fires and other activities by the Jalisco New Generation Cartel, and American tourists were told to shelter in place and avoid areas of law enforcement activity.

item.title: Wiener Introduces New State Legislation That Would Allow Cities to 'Breakup with PG&E' and Start Their Own Public Utilities
item.description: State Senator Scott Wiener is trying to bolster his run for Congress with a new bill targeting PG&E, a bill that would allow cities to "breakup with PG&E." But does deficit-strapped SF even have the money to do this?

item.title: BART Takes Steps to Clear Encampments Near Tracks After Sunday Fire Causes Service Meltdown
item.description: BART says it is now working with the City of Oakland to "proactively address" other spots where homeless encampment fires could potentially threaten train service.

item.title: Yet Another SF Nonprofit CEO, Who Allegedly Stole $1.2 Million, Criminally Charged With Misuse of Public Money
item.description: Criminal charges just came down on a former SF homelessness nonprofit CEO accused of buying a Tesla with public money, among a slew of other financial improprieties, and she's facing nine felony charges.

item.title: The Slanted Door Group Says Restaurant Will Return to Valencia Street Next Year
item.description: A little over a year after the unexpected death of founder and chef Charles Phan, The Slanted Door Group is ready to get rolling on realizing his vision to return to the Valencia Street space where it all started.

item.title: Third Suspect Charged In Early January Oakland Triple-Homicide, Which Police Say Was Over a $10 Bag of Weed
item.description: A measly dime-bag of pot deal gone wrong left three men dead in Oakland last month, and now the marijuana dealer has been arrested too, but boy did he have a lengthy list of priors.

item.title: Day Around the Bay: El Mencho Got His Start Selling Drugs In SF at Age 19
item.description: The Mexican cartel leader who was killed Sunday was arrested selling drugs in SF in 1986; the 'bring cars back to the Great Highway' ballot measure has filed paperwork; and Oakland is slowly on the hunt for a new police chief.
